title: 2-Year FRN auction (NEW ISSUE) — stamps the spread both 2027 reopenings inherit, on an FOMC decision day the record says costs it nothing
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched by plain curl and re-derived independently 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), text layer inflated stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 auction records. Row reads `2-Year FRN / Announcement Thursday, January 21, 2027 / Auction Wednesday, January 27, 2027 / Settlement Monday, February 01, 2027`. THE MISSING `R` IS THE POINT and it was verified at the token level this session, not read off the proposal: the PDF's own legend reads `R --denotes reopening`, and in the raw item stream the 2026-08-26, 2026-09-23, 2026-11-24 and 2026-12-17 FRN rows are each followed by a standalone `R` token while the 2026-10-22 and 2027-01-21 rows are followed directly by their announcement date. So Treasury marks this a NEW ISSUE. Stays estimate on the same two counts the sibling FRN entries record: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2027-01-21 announcement itself. The `TSY:` confirmed prefix in market-events-data.ts covers a treasury.gov auction schedule and is deliberately NOT taken for those two reasons.
notes: Canonical file written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09) after reading its single proposal, proposals/treasury-2y-frn-2027-01-27.from-treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-21.json, in full. THE HEADLINE, AND IT CORRECTS THE PROPOSAL THAT CREATED THIS ENTRY: the proposer registered that FRN new issues selling on an FOMC decision day see BETTER demand (bid-to-cover 3.363 on the 15 decision-day new issues against 3.096 for the other 32, 'higher, not lower'). Re-derived this session from the full 154-auction FRN series (auctions_query floating_rate:Yes, HTTP 200, 532,321 bytes) joined to 107 FOMC statement dates parsed from federalreserve.gov's own calendars (fomccalendars.htm plus fomchistorical2014-2020, all HTTP 200), the pooled gap is even larger — 3.543 (n=18) against 3.143 (n=33), Welch t = +2.32, and it survives dropping the 5.67 outlier at t = +2.23. IT DOES NOT SURVIVE CONTROLLING FOR THE YEAR. Year-demeaned, the cover gap collapses from t = +2.32 to t = +0.63 and the tail gap from t = -1.57 to t = -1.02; within-year the cover difference is positive in only 3 of the 8 years that carry both kinds, mean +0.098. The cause is a composition shift in the auction calendar, not a decision-day effect: 2014 and 2015 put 7 of their 8 new issues on decision days at mean covers of 4.50 and 3.64, while 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2024 put ZERO of their 16 on one at 3.29, 2.72, 3.19 and 3.29. Pooling those eras is Simpson's paradox. The honest reading is a NULL on both price and demand — which is the strongest possible form of 'read it, do not trade it' for this event. SECOND, AND THE REASON THE COLLISION EXISTS AT ALL: it is a weekday artifact, total in both directions. All 18 decision-day FRN new issues fell on a WEDNESDAY (18 of the 40 Wednesday new issues, 45%); NONE of the 10 Tuesday new issues did, and 9 of those 10 sold exactly ONE DAY BEFORE a decision (2024-10-29 the sole exception, +9d). Only 1 of 103 reopenings ever landed on a decision day. So 27 of 51 new issues (53%) sit on the decision day or the day before it, and which one is decided entirely by the weekday Treasury assigns inside the month-end note week of January, April, July and October — the same last week in which the FOMC schedules its Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct meeting. All 51 new issues fall in those four months (13/13/13/12). THIRD, THE STRUCTURAL FACT WORTH MORE THAN THE FOMC FRAMING: this is the SPREAD-STAMPING auction of the quarter. At a new issue the auction's high discount margin IS the spread — the two fields are identical on all 51 — and every one of the 103 reopenings in the series carries the spread its own new issue stamped, 103 of 103 matched by original_issue_date. Whatever clears here is the coupon spread both 2027 reopenings inherit for the life of the note. FOURTH, MECHANICAL: the same-day slate on 2027-01-27 is TWO auctions (this FRN plus a 17-week bill) read from the PDF's own rows, so the congestion rule inherited from treasury-2y-frn-2026-11-24 predicts a `11:30 AM` close — 27 of 27 among two-auction new issues, 68 of 68 across all FRN two-auction days. An FOMC decision day does not move the close either: 18 of the 19 decision-day FRN auctions closed at 11:30 a.m. FIFTH: the index rate derives to 2027-01-25. The settlement-precedence rule (most recent Monday 13-week bill auctioned before the FRN whose settlement precedes the FRN's) reproduces at 152 of 154 against the full bill series (HTTP 200, 502,593 bytes), with both misses named and both of them TUESDAY auctions — on WEDNESDAY auctions, which this is, it is 125 of 125. The Monday 2027-01-25 bill settles 2027-01-28, before this FRN's 2027-02-01 settlement; the 2027-02-01 bill settles 2027-02-04 and is excluded. NOTE THE ORDERING IS THE ORDINARY ONE, NOT THE THANKSGIVING SIBLING'S: the index (01-25) is set AFTER the 01-21 announcement, so a lane inheriting treasury-2y-frn-2026-11-24's 'index locked before the announcement' framing has it backwards here. The MLK holiday on 2027-01-18 shifts that week's bill slate to Tuesday 01-19 but does not touch the index, because 01-25 is a later Monday. SIXTH: size expectation $30B, 10 of the last 10 new issues since 2024-04-24, and a lane inheriting the 2026-11-19 sibling's $28B reopening figure would be wrong by $2B. SEVENTH: this auction settles 2027-02-01, five days out, with the month-end 2-Year and 5-Year notes rather than at the usual T+2 — the modal January gap (5 days in 2015, 2016, 2021, 2022 and 2026). ONE-YEAR ANALOG, row for row: 2026-01-28, a Wednesday decision day with a two-auction slate, closed 11:30 a.m., stamped spread 0.099, cover 3.16, tail 0.014, indirect 61.4%. FORWARD OBSERVATION, not registrable yet: if Treasury keeps the Wednesday slot, all four 2027 FRN new issues collide with decision days (Jan 27, Apr 28, Jul 28, Oct 27 against FOMC Jan 26-27, Apr 27-28, Jul 27-28, Oct 26-27 read from federalreserve.gov 2026-09-09), but the tentative schedule ends at 2027-01-27 so only this one is documented. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. Three forward tests registered in this event's own fragment, all scoring 2027-01-28: -1 the closing time reads `11:30 AM`, -2 frn_index_determination_date reads 2027-01-25, -3 the decision-day null holds, i.e. the print lands inside the last-twelve-new-issue envelope on both tail (<= 0.030) and cover (>= 2.69).
